# Configuration Reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_config_reference.py from the configuration
models; do not edit by hand. Run the script after changing a config field. -->

> 🇰🇷 한국어 사용자 가이드: [docs/user-guide.ko.md §2](./user-guide.ko.md#2-설정)
> (this reference is generated in English only)

Every configuration key, its type, its built-in default and what it does,
one table per section. How the configuration is loaded (file, `backend`
preset, environment, CLI flags) and the settings most runs change are in the
[User Guide §2](./user-guide.md#2-configuration);
[`config-template.yaml`](../config-template.yaml) is a commented starting file.

- **Defaults** are the built-in values a key takes when the file, the
  environment and the flags leave it unset. `null` usually means "derived":
  the description says from what.
- **Environment.** Any key can be set as `UKR__` followed by its path in
  upper case with `__` between the segments, for example
  `UKR__AWS__NEPTUNE__ENDPOINT` for `aws.neptune.endpoint`; a list or
  mapping value takes JSON. The standard AWS variables also apply when nothing else sets the key: `AWS_PROFILE` fills `aws.profile_name`, `AWS_REGION` fills `aws.region_name`.
- **Unknown keys** fail the load (`--allow-unknown-keys` turns that into a
  warning). Keys that moved are refused with their new place; see
  [Moved keys](#moved-keys).

## Top-level keys

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backend` | `"aws"` \| `"local"` | `"aws"` | Provider preset. 'aws' (default): Bedrock, Neptune, OpenSearch and DynamoDB. 'local': fills in local providers (Ollama, a cross-encoder reranker, embedded SQLite graph/vector stores and registry) for every providers/aws.neptune/aws.opensearch key the config leaves unset. |

## `providers`

Per-role provider selection (models, stores, registry)

### `providers.llm`

Language-model provider

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | string \| null (min length 1) | `null` | Endpoint of the model server, e.g. http://localhost:11434 for Ollama or http://localhost:8000/v1 for an OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio). Ignored by bedrock. |
| `api_key` | secret string \| null | `null` | API key for an OpenAI-compatible server (masked in logs). Most local servers ignore it; null sends a placeholder. Ignored by bedrock and ollama. |
| `timeout_seconds` | number (> 0) | `300.0` | HTTP timeout per request to the model server, in seconds. |
| `max_attempts` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Attempts per request on transient errors, including the first. The OpenAI client retries itself; on Ollama, whose client does not, query chains and embedding calls are retried by the framework (ingestion chains keep processing.max_attempts). 1 disables the retry. |
| `kind` | string (min length 1) | `"bedrock"` | Language-model provider: bedrock \| openai_compatible \| ollama. |
| `context_window_size` | integer (≥ 1024) | `32768` | Context window of the non-Bedrock models, in tokens. Sizes the retrieval context budget and is sent to Ollama as num_ctx. Bedrock models take theirs from the capability catalog. |
| `max_output_tokens` | integer (≥ 1) | `8192` | Output-token ceiling of the non-Bedrock models. A request asks for aws.bedrock.default_max_output_tokens (or a prompt's own floor), clamped to this. |
| `temperature` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 2.0) | `0.0` | Sampling temperature for the non-Bedrock models. |
| `tokenizer` | `"estimate"` \| `"tiktoken"` | `"estimate"` | Token counting for the non-Bedrock models: 'estimate' (the script-aware estimate Bedrock also falls back to) or 'tiktoken' (needs the [local] extra; tiktoken downloads its encoding file on first use). Falls back to the estimate when tiktoken is unavailable. |
| `tiktoken_encoding` | string (min length 1) | `"cl100k_base"` | tiktoken encoding name used when tokenizer is 'tiktoken'. |

## `models`

Which model serves each role, on the providers above

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | string \| null (min length 1) | `null` | Model of the 'default' tier (extraction, gleaning, claims, community reports, output fixing, query entity/keyword extraction, answer generation, evaluation). null = anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5 on Bedrock; required with another provider. |
| `fast` | string \| null (min length 1) | `null` | Model of the 'fast' tier (chunking, translation, description summarization, global/DRIFT search steps, query translation, rewriting and routing). null = anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5 on Bedrock, the default tier's model with another provider. |
| `rerank` | `"amazon.rerank-v1:0"` \| `"cohere.rerank-v3-5:0"` \| string \| null | `null` | Rerank model. Bedrock: one of the RerankModelId values, null = cohere.rerank-v3-5:0. cross_encoder: a sentence-transformers model name, required. Ignored with providers.rerank.kind none. |

The embedding model and its dimension.

## `aws`

AWS services configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region_name` | string (min length 1) | `"us-west-2"` | Region of Neptune, OpenSearch, S3 and DynamoDB, and of Bedrock unless aws.bedrock.region_name is set. AWS_REGION fills it only when the file leaves it unset. The default offers every default model, including both rerank models, which some regions (e.g. ap-northeast-2) do not. |
| `profile_name` | string \| null | `null` | Named AWS profile. null uses the default credential chain (environment variables, instance or task role, ...); AWS_PROFILE fills it only when the file leaves it unset. |

### `aws.bedrock`

AWS Bedrock service configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region_name` | string \| null (min length 1) | `null` | Region for Bedrock model, embedding and rerank calls, and where the guardrail must exist. null = aws.region_name. Set it only when your models are enabled in another region; in a private VPC whose only Bedrock route is a VPC endpoint, leave it null or set the VPC's region. |
| `assumed_role_arn` | string \| null | `null` | AWS assumed role ARN for Bedrock service |
| `enable_global_profile` | boolean | `true` | Resolve cross-region (global) inference profiles. Keep it on: Claude 4.7+ and OpenAI GPT models are invocable only through a profile, which also needs bedrock:ListInferenceProfiles. |
| `default_max_output_tokens` | integer \| null (≥ 1) | `16384` | max_tokens sent with each LLM request, clamped to the model's maximum. Bedrock reserves input + max_tokens against the tokens-per-minute quota when a request starts, so sending the model maximum (128K on Claude 5.x) throttles concurrent calls long before real usage does. Thinking tokens count toward it. Prompts with long outputs (graph/claim extraction, gleaning, community reports, document translation) declare a higher floor that wins over this value. Raise it if answers are cut off (stopReason max_tokens); null sends the model maximum. |
| `model_overrides` | dict[string, dict[string, Any]] | `{}` | Per-model capability overrides keyed by model id, e.g. {'amazon.nova-pro-v1:0': {'context_window_size': 300000}}. Keys are capability-record fields (context_window_size, max_output_tokens, supports_thinking, supports_sampling_params, supports_prompt_caching, ...). Use it for a model without a curated record, or to correct one, without a release. Language models only: embedding and rerank ids are a closed list (EmbeddingModelId, RerankModelId). |
| `enable_1m_context` | boolean | `false` | Opt into the 1M-token context window on models that support it as a beta (Claude Sonnet 4 / 4.5, Opus 4 / 4.1 / 4.5). Off by default: long-context requests are billed at a premium on those models. Claude 5 has a native 1M window and ignores this flag. Enabling it also widens the derived retrieval context budget. |
| `default_effort` | `"low"` \| `"medium"` \| `"high"` \| `"xhigh"` \| `"max"` | `"high"` | Reasoning effort for calls on the default tier's model (models.default). Sent as output_config.effort to Anthropic adaptive-thinking models (Claude 4.6+), where it replaces the fixed thinking token budget, and as reasoning.effort to OpenAI GPT models. 'xhigh'/'max' are only accepted by some models, and an unsupported level fails fast; lower it to cut cost and latency. |
| `fast_effort` | `"low"` \| `"medium"` \| `"high"` \| `"xhigh"` \| `"max"` | `"low"` | Reasoning effort for calls on the fast tier's model (models.fast; when it differs from the default tier's). The shipped fast model, Claude Haiku 5.5, thinks adaptively, so this sets how much it reasons on fast-tier calls; it has no effect on a fast model that does not reason. |
| `ingestion_effort` | `"low"` \| `"medium"` \| `"high"` \| `"xhigh"` \| `"max"` \| null | `null` | Reasoning effort for ingestion calls on the default tier (graph extraction, gleaning, claim extraction, community reports, prompt tuning, and the output fixer when models.roles.fixing is a default-tier model). These make up most of an ingestion's default-tier tokens, so lowering this cuts ingestion cost without changing query-time effort. null inherits default_effort. Fast-tier ingestion calls keep fast_effort. |

#### `aws.bedrock.guardrail`

Amazon Bedrock Guardrails configuration (disabled unless identifier set)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identifier` | string \| null | `null` | Bedrock guardrail ID or ARN; setting it enables the guardrail on the query path. The guardrail must exist in aws.bedrock.region_name. |
| `version` | string (min length 1) | `"DRAFT"` | Guardrail version to apply (e.g. 'DRAFT' or a published version number) |
| `trace` | boolean | `false` | Emit guardrail trace details for observability/auditing (full assessments, including non-detected entries) |
| `check_input` | boolean | `true` | Screen each raw user query (ApplyGuardrail, source INPUT) before retrieval: prompt attacks, denied topics, PII |
| `check_output` | boolean | `true` | Screen each final answer (ApplyGuardrail, source OUTPUT). A streamed answer is then delivered in one chunk, after the check |

#### `aws.bedrock.transient_retry`

Retry for embedding and query-time LLM calls on transient Bedrock errors

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_attempts` | integer (≥ 1) | `5` | Attempts per call, including the first, for transient Bedrock errors that botocore does not retry (such as HTTP 424), on embeddings and query-time calls. 1 disables the retry. |
| `base_delay_seconds` | number (≥ 0.0) | `2.0` | Backoff ceiling for the first retry; doubles per attempt with equal jitter |
| `max_delay_seconds` | number (≥ 0.0) | `16.0` | Upper bound on a single backoff delay in seconds |
| `max_total_seconds` | number (≥ 0.0) | `60.0` | Wall-clock retry budget per call; no retry starts once the next backoff would cross it |

### `aws.neptune`

AWS Neptune database configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string \| null | `null` | Neptune cluster endpoint. Required with the neptune graph store (the CDK stack injects it as UKR__AWS__NEPTUNE__ENDPOINT). |
| `port` | integer (≥ 1, ≤ 65535) | `8182` | Neptune database connection port |
| `use_iam` | boolean | `true` | SigV4-sign Neptune requests (IAM database authentication). |
| `use_ssl` | boolean | `true` | Connect over TLS (wss://). Neptune requires it; set false only for a plain TinkerPop Gremlin Server (ws://), together with use_iam: false. |
| `pool_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `4` | Gremlin DriverRemoteConnection pool size (max concurrent in-flight requests over the websocket). The client raises it to indexing.neptune.index_concurrency when that is larger, so concurrent write batches are not serialized on fewer connections. Query traversals beyond it wait on the event loop. The default matches the 4 query threads (2 x vCPUs) of the default db.r6g.large instance; more in-flight requests only queue on the server, so raise it with the instance size. |

### `aws.opensearch`

AWS OpenSearch service configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string \| null | `null` | OpenSearch domain endpoint. Required with the opensearch vector store (the CDK stack injects it as UKR__AWS__OPENSEARCH__ENDPOINT). |
| `port` | integer (≥ 1, ≤ 65535) | `443` | OpenSearch cluster connection port |
| `username` | string \| null | `null` | OpenSearch authentication username |
| `password` | secret string \| null | `null` | OpenSearch authentication password (masked in logs/repr) |
| `use_ssl` | boolean | `true` | Enable SSL/TLS connection |
| `verify_certs` | boolean | `true` | Verify SSL/TLS certificates |
| `use_iam` | boolean | `false` | SigV4-sign OpenSearch requests. false uses basic auth with username / password, usually from UKR__AWS__OPENSEARCH__USERNAME and UKR__AWS__OPENSEARCH__PASSWORD (for example in .env). |
| `allow_anonymous` | boolean | `false` | Connect without authentication, for a local OpenSearch with the security plugin disabled. Mutually exclusive with use_iam and username/password. |
| `sigv4_service_name` | string | `"es"` | SigV4 signing service for IAM auth: 'es' for a managed OpenSearch domain, 'aoss' for an OpenSearch Serverless collection. A wrong value fails auth (often surfacing as zero search hits). |

## `fixing`

Output fixing configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | When a structured stage gets malformed JSON from the model, ask a model (models.roles.fixing) to repair it instead of failing the item. Leave it on. |

## `processing`

Text processing configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_concurrency` | integer (≥ 1) | `40` | LLM calls an ingestion stage keeps in flight: the next item starts as soon as one finishes, so this is both the peak and the steady concurrency. These stages are I/O-bound, so this can be well above the CPU count. Bedrock quotas differ per account, model and Region: lower it if the logs show ThrottlingException retries, raise it if quota allows. The backend: local preset sets 20, since a local model server queues the calls it cannot run at once. |
| `max_attempts` | integer (≥ 1) | `5` | Attempts per ingestion LLM item, including the first call. Transient Bedrock errors, call timeouts and unparseable output are retried; other errors fail fast. 1 disables the retry. |
| `io_workers` | integer (≥ 1) | `64` | Threads for blocking I/O on the query path (the Bedrock calls LangChain runs in the event loop's default executor, Neptune traversals, reranking) in the CLIs and GraphRAGChain's sync methods. Python's default is min(32, CPUs + 4), six on a 2-vCPU task. An async host calls unified_kg_rag.configure_event_loop(asyncio.get_running_loop(), config.processing.io_workers) at startup. |
| `ignore_errors` | boolean | `false` | When a whole step fails (a batch call, a translation language, an evaluator, global map/reduce, the DRIFT primer, the auto router), log it and continue with an empty or degraded result instead of raising. Items whose own LLM call fails are always skipped and reported, whatever this says. |
| `deduplicate` | boolean | `false` | Drop near-duplicate documents before extraction. Two documents are near-duplicates when the Jaccard similarity of their character 3-gram sets, estimated with a 128-permutation MinHash, is at least 0.9 (fixed parameters); of each pair the first is kept, and an incremental run keeps the already-indexed copy. |
| `resolution_method` | `"minhash"` \| `"sequence_matcher"` | `"minhash"` | Name-similarity measure of fuzzy entity resolution (fuzzy_entity_resolution): minhash or sequence_matcher. |
| `fuzzy_entity_resolution` | boolean | `false` | Also merge entities whose names are only similar (resolution_method at similarity_threshold), in full builds and incremental merges alike. Off by default: names are merged when they are equal after normalization, legal-form removal ('Acme Inc' / 'Acme') and dense-script spacing, because name similarity also joins different organizations that share most of their name ('... University' / '... University Hospital'). |
| `similarity_threshold` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.85` | Similarity threshold for fuzzy entity resolution (fuzzy_entity_resolution) and for matching claim subjects and objects to entity names. Raise it if distinct entities merge. |

### `processing.document_parsing`

Document parsing configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source_directory` | string \| path | `"source"` | Directory to load documents from, for library callers. run-ingestion requires --source-directory (or UKR_SOURCE_DIRECTORY) instead. |
| `target_directory` | string \| path \| null | `null` | Directory to export each parsed document to as <stem>.json for inspection (run-ingestion --output-directory). null = no export. Must not be the source directory. |
| `index_value` | string \| null | `null` | Index suffix the run writes: every OpenSearch index and Neptune label is named <prefix>-<index_value>. null = 'default'. Query the corpus with the same value as run-rag / run-eval --suffix. run-ingestion has no flag for it: use one config file per tenant or corpus version. |
| `source_scope` | string \| null | `null` | Identity of the corpus source for incremental indexing: a run only treats registry documents of its own index suffix AND source scope as deleted. None = the resolved source directory. Set it when the local directory is a staging copy, e.g. the S3 URI a container syncs from (env UKR__PROCESSING__DOCUMENT_PARSING__SOURCE_SCOPE). |

### `processing.chunking`

Text chunking configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chunker_type` | `"simple"` \| `"intelligent"` | `"intelligent"` | intelligent lets the chunking model pick semantic boundaries (one fast LLM call per pre-chunk); simple splits by size with no LLM call. |
| `min_chunk_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `1000` | Minimum chunk size in characters; shorter pieces are merged into a neighbour. Default 1,000 (~250 English tokens) keeps headings and short trailing paragraphs from becoming chunks of their own. |
| `max_chunk_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `8000` | Maximum chunk size in characters. Every chunk is embedded whole and reranked as one document, so it must fit the embedding model's input (Titan Text Embeddings V2: 8,192 tokens) and the reranker's per-document limit (Cohere Rerank 3.5: 4,096 tokens), or its tail is never embedded or reranked. Sizes count characters: English averages ~4 characters per token, a Han/Hangul/Kana character ~1, so for CJK corpora with reranking use about half the default sizes. |
| `chunk_overlap` | integer (≥ 0) | `500` | Overlap between consecutive chunks, in characters. |
| `pre_chunk_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `50000` | Pre-chunk size in characters: the window the intelligent chunker's LLM picks boundaries in. Not embedded itself (its chunks are capped by max_chunk_size), so it is sized for the chunking model's prompt. |
| `pre_chunk_overlap` | integer (≥ 0) | `500` | Pre-chunk overlap in characters |
| `fallback_chunk_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `4800` | Target chunk size for the size-based splitter (the simple chunker, and intelligent chunking when the LLM fails or a chunk exceeds max_chunk_size). It splits at paragraphs, then lines, then after CJK sentence terminators, then spaces. 4,800 characters is ~1,200 English tokens, the default chunk size of MS GraphRAG and LightRAG. |
| `max_marker_miss_rate` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.1` | Maximum allowed boundary marker miss rate |

### `processing.translation`

Text translation configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Run the translation stage. It is skipped at no cost when source_language equals target_language and there are no additional_target_languages. |
| `source_language` | `"de"` \| `"en"` \| `"es"` \| `"fr"` \| `"it"` \| `"ja"` \| `"ko"` \| `"pt"` \| `"ru"` \| `"zh"` | `"en"` | Predominant source language of the corpus. Selects the OpenSearch analyzer of the original chunk text and drives the same-language no-op skip; translation itself is content-driven. |
| `target_language` | `"de"` \| `"en"` \| `"es"` \| `"fr"` \| `"it"` \| `"ja"` \| `"ko"` \| `"pt"` \| `"ru"` \| `"zh"` | `"en"` | Language the corpus is translated into. Extraction, embeddings and the answer context use it, and entity and relationship descriptions are written in it. |
| `additional_target_languages` | list[`"de"` \| `"en"` \| `"es"` \| `"fr"` \| `"it"` \| `"ja"` \| `"ko"` \| `"pt"` \| `"ru"` \| `"zh"`] \| null | `null` | Extra languages to translate into. Each is indexed in its own translated_text_<language> field with that language's analyzer and searched lexically (useful with a per-query RAGInput.target_language); extraction, embeddings and the answer context use target_language only. Each language is one more LLM call per chunk. |

### `processing.graph_extraction`

Graph extraction configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_entities_per_chunk` | integer (≥ 1) | `50` | Most entities the extraction prompt asks for per text chunk; it also sizes the extraction call's output-token floor. |
| `max_relationships_per_chunk` | integer (≥ 1) | `50` | Maximum relationships per text chunk |
| `entity_confidence_threshold` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.0` | Drop an entity from each chunk that scored it below this confidence, with that chunk's relationships naming it (per chunk, so the result does not depend on which documents are indexed together). Compared against the normalized confidence: the prompt's 1-10 score / 10. 0.0 keeps everything. |
| `entity_types` | list[string] | see `config-template.yaml` | Entity categories injected into the extraction prompt, each 'LABEL: short description' (the description is optional), e.g. ['GENE: ...', 'DISEASE: ...']. The cheapest and most effective domain-adaptation knob; an empty list lets the model choose any relevant types. |

#### `processing.graph_extraction.description_summarization`

LLM re-summarization of over-long merged descriptions

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Re-summarize merged descriptions longer than force_summary_threshold_tokens with an LLM (as MS GraphRAG and LightRAG do). Off, descriptions are only concatenated and grow without bound for frequently mentioned entities. |
| `force_summary_threshold_tokens` | integer (≥ 1) | `600` | Re-summarize a merged description only when its estimated token count exceeds this threshold. Descriptions at or below it are left as-is, so cheap entities never incur an LLM call. |
| `max_summary_tokens` | integer (≥ 1) | `256` | Target length (in tokens) of the produced summary; injected into the summarization prompt as the budget. |

#### `processing.graph_extraction.entity_grounding`

Provenance grounding guard against hallucinated entities

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Hallucination guard: drop (or, with action 'penalize', down-weight) entities and relationships whose verbatim source_text span is not found in their chunk. Punctuation is ignored and Han/Hangul/Kana spans are compared by character bigrams, so a changed Korean particle still counts as present. It applies to gleaning additions too. Requires an extraction model that emits a source_text span per item. |
| `action` | string | `"drop"` | What to do with an ungrounded entity: 'drop' removes it; 'penalize' multiplies its confidence by penalty_factor so the confidence threshold can filter it without hard deletion. An ungrounded relationship is likewise dropped, or kept at its weight times penalty_factor; 'penalize' still drops one naming an entity its chunk did not extract, which it would otherwise make cite the chunk. Gleaning additions follow the same action. |
| `penalty_factor` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.5` | Confidence multiplier applied to ungrounded entities when action='penalize'. |
| `min_span_tokens` | integer (≥ 1) | `4` | Evidence spans shorter than this (after normalization) are treated as grounded — too short to judge, so the gate never deletes short legitimate names on weak signal. A Han/Hangul/Kana character counts as one token. |
| `min_overlap_ratio` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.6` | When the span is not a verbatim substring, the fraction of its tokens that must appear in the chunk to still count as grounded (handles light paraphrase / whitespace edits). |

### `processing.gleaning`

Iterative extraction refinement configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Extra extraction passes per text unit that ask the model for the entities and relationships it missed. |
| `max_rounds` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Maximum gleaning rounds per text unit. Each round after the first re-sends only the text units whose previous answer added a new entity or relationship, so a unit stops once an answer adds nothing new. 1 is MS GraphRAG's default, for when ingestion cost matters more than graph recall. |
| `max_entities_per_prompt` | integer (≥ 1) | `100` | Maximum entities per gleaning prompt |
| `max_relationships_per_prompt` | integer (≥ 1) | `100` | Maximum relationships per gleaning prompt |

### `processing.claim_extraction`

Claim extraction configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Extract claims (covariates): one more LLM call per text unit. When on, local search injects the matching claims into its context and simple search includes the claims index in its sweep. Claim subjects and objects are not linked into the entity graph. |
| `max_entities_per_prompt` | integer (≥ 0) | `100` | Maximum entities per claim extraction prompt |

## `graph`

Graph analysis configuration

### `graph.analysis`

Graph analysis configuration

#### `graph.analysis.statistics`

Graph-level statistics configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `calculate_density` | boolean | `true` | Calculate graph density to measure network connectivity |
| `calculate_clustering` | boolean | `true` | Calculate clustering coefficient to measure local connectivity |
| `calculate_diameter` | boolean | `false` | Calculate graph diameter (computationally expensive) |
| `calculate_components` | boolean | `true` | Analyze connected components to identify isolated subgraphs |

### `graph.community_detection`

Community detection configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Run Leiden community detection + LLM community-report generation during indexing. Required for GraphRAG global/drift search. Disable for a lighter, LightRAG-only ingestion (mix/hybrid/naive need only entities, relationships, and the relationship vector index — no communities), which skips the Leiden pass and all report LLM calls. |
| `resolution` | number (> 0.0, ≤ 10.0) | `1.0` | Leiden modularity resolution: higher gives more, smaller communities (and more report calls); lower gives fewer, larger ones. |
| `random_state` | integer (≥ 1) | `42` | Leiden random seed (a positive integer; the native Leiden rejects 0). The same graph and seed give the same communities. |
| `max_levels` | integer (≥ 1) | `5` | Maximum depth of the community hierarchy. |
| `trials` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Number of independent Leiden runs to find best partition |
| `extra_forced_iterations` | integer (≥ 0) | `2` | Additional optimization iterations after convergence |
| `max_cluster_size` | integer (≥ 2) | `20` | Maximum members per community: entities at level 0, child communities above. A larger Leiden community is re-partitioned on its own subgraph, recursively, until every piece fits or Leiden finds no finer split; the next level regroups the pieces. Without the bound, modularity's resolution limit grows communities with the corpus beyond what one report's max_report_context_tokens can describe (or a parent's roll-up can summarize). MS GraphRAG's default is 10 with a larger report budget; 20 typically keeps a leaf's entities and relationships, or a parent's child summaries, within the default 4000-token report context. |
| `min_community_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Minimum entities per level-0 community: a smaller one merges into the neighbour it shares the most edge weight with, unless that would exceed max_cluster_size. A connected component of fewer entities (an isolated entity, a pair) has no neighbour and gets no community or report. 1 = cluster every component. |
| `auto_resolution` | boolean | `false` | Sweep auto_resolution_candidates at every hierarchy level and keep the most modular resolution; otherwise resolution is used. Off by default: maximizing modularity on the coarse upper-level graphs picks low resolutions that merge unrelated communities, which cost global search accuracy in testing. |
| `auto_resolution_candidates` | list[number] | `[0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0]` | Resolution values swept when auto_resolution is enabled; the one maximizing modularity is chosen. |
| `auto_resolution_max_nodes` | integer (≥ 1) | `10000` | Skip the auto_resolution sweep (which runs one full Leiden partition + modularity computation per candidate, ~10x the base cost, at every hierarchy level) when the graph exceeds this many nodes, and use the fixed `resolution` instead. Prevents the sweep from dominating the analysis phase on large graphs. Raise to force the sweep on bigger graphs. |

#### `graph.community_detection.report_generation`

Community report generation configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Enable automatic community report generation |
| `max_entities_per_report` | integer (≥ 1) | `50` | Maximum entities per community report |
| `max_report_context_tokens` | integer (≥ 1) | `4000` | Token budget for the entity/relationship context packed into a community report prompt. Entities are degree-sorted (most connected first) and packed up to this budget, so truncation drops the least-important entities first. max_entities_per_report remains an additional upper bound on entity count. |
| `content_length` | string | `"medium"` | Report length, as the number of findings the report asks for: short (5-7), medium (7-10), long (10-15) |
| `enable_sub_community_rollup` | boolean | `true` | When a parent community's raw entity/relationship context would exceed max_report_context_tokens, substitute summaries of its already-generated child sub-community reports for the lowest-priority raw context (MS GraphRAG parity), instead of simply truncating. Requires bottom-up per-level report generation (level 0 = finest first). Set false to keep the flat, truncate-on-overflow behaviour. |

### `graph.visualization`

Visualization configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Render visualizations during ingestion. Off by default: it adds an embedding call per node (embedding_method) and a dimensionality reduction to every ingest; render on demand with run-visualization from the data export_data writes instead. |
| `export_data` | boolean | `true` | Write visualization_data.json (graph nodes, edges and the community hierarchy) at ingestion when enabled is false, so run-visualization can render on demand. One pass over the graph: no embedding or model call, no layout or centrality (run-visualization computes them). enabled: true always writes the file, with its layout. |
| `outputs_directory` | string \| path \| null | `null` | Directory to save visualization files. When unset, ingestion writes to '<cache directory>/<pipeline_id>/visualization' (--cache-directory), so visualization_data.json is synced to S3 with the cache; other callers fall back to 'outputs/visualization'. |
| `embedding_method` | string | `"description"` | Node embedding for the layout: 'description' embeds each node's 'name: description' with the embedding model; 'none' uses a spring layout from the graph topology. |
| `layout_method` | string | `"umap"` | Dimensionality reduction of the node layout: umap, tsne or pca. |

#### `graph.visualization.centrality`

Node centrality metrics the visualization sizes nodes and plots by (computed at render time; no ingestion stage reads them)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `calculate_degree` | boolean | `true` | Calculate degree centrality to measure node connectivity |
| `calculate_betweenness` | boolean | `true` | Compute betweenness centrality (bridge nodes) for the visualization; ingestion itself computes no centrality. On graphs larger than betweenness_auto_sample_threshold nodes it is sampled instead of computed exactly. |
| `calculate_pagerank` | boolean | `true` | Calculate PageRank centrality to rank node importance |
| `calculate_closeness` | boolean | `false` | Calculate closeness centrality to measure node proximity |
| `calculate_eigenvector` | boolean | `false` | Calculate eigenvector centrality to measure influence based on connections |
| `pagerank_alpha` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.85` | PageRank damping factor |
| `pagerank_max_iter` | integer (≥ 1) | `100` | Maximum iterations for PageRank convergence |
| `betweenness_k` | integer \| null (≥ 1) | `null` | Sample size for betweenness calculation (None for all nodes) |
| `betweenness_auto_sample_threshold` | integer (≥ 1) | `2000` | When betweenness_k is None (exact) AND the graph has more nodes than this, automatically switch to sampled betweenness (using this value as the pivot-sample size) instead of exact all-pairs shortest paths. Exact betweenness is O(V*E) and stalls on large real graphs; sampling keeps the analysis phase bounded. Raise this to force exact computation on larger graphs. |
| `betweenness_seed` | integer | `42` | Random seed for sampled betweenness (only used when betweenness_k is set). Fixed for reproducibility — sampled betweenness picks random pivots, so without a seed centrality is non-deterministic. |
| `eigenvector_max_iter` | integer (≥ 1) | `1000` | Maximum iterations for eigenvector centrality convergence |
| `eigenvector_tol` | number (> 0.0) | `0.001` | Convergence tolerance for eigenvector centrality |

## `indexing`

Data indexing configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reset` | boolean | `false` | Rebuild the run's index namespace from the whole corpus instead of applying a delta, without taking it offline: the vector indices swap aliases, the graph is rewritten in place and what the rebuild did not write is dropped at the end; then the namespace's registry records are written again. Set it for one run. |
| `additional_suffix` | string \| null (min length 1) | `null` | Appended after the run's suffix in every OpenSearch index name and Neptune label (<prefix>-<suffix>-<additional_suffix>; the suffix is processing.document_parsing.index_value at ingestion and --suffix at query time, both 'default' when unset). Set it identically for ingestion and queries, for versioned or multi-tenant separation. |
| `community_drift_threshold` | number (> 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.5` | On incremental runs with communities on, recommend a rebuild (WARNING and the community_rebuild_recommended metric) when at least this share of the entities the run clustered also belongs to an earlier level-0 community. A delta run clusters only its own documents, so such an entity sits in two communities and the earlier community's report misses what the run added; indexing.reset: true re-clusters the whole graph. |
| `max_failure_rate` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.2` | Per-index-type write failure rate above which the indexing stage fails, and share of communities without a report above which community detection fails; below it the affected documents are recorded FAILED and retried. A fully failed index type always fails the stage. 1.0 disables the partial-failure gate. |
| `max_document_failures` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Incremental runs: a document recorded FAILED this many consecutive runs with unchanged content is no longer retried. It stays FAILED and is skipped as unchanged (with a WARNING) until its content changes or this value is raised. |
| `max_document_attempts` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Incremental runs: once runs died this many consecutive times (the task was killed; a stopped or failed run does not count) processing a document's unchanged content, the runs isolate it: a document that died processed alone is quarantined (the next run removes what the attempts wrote, records it QUARANTINED and skips it until its content or the extraction settings change or this value is raised); otherwise the next runs process half of the documents it died with and defer the other new and changed documents until the culprit is alone. |
| `lease_seconds` | number (≥ 10.0) | `300.0` | Incremental runs: the term of an index namespace's write lease, which a run holds from its first stage to its end so no other run writes the namespace meanwhile. The run renews it every sixth of the term and stops writing once less than a third is left since its last renewal (keep it at least three times the longest store write request); a run that dies stops renewing, so its lease expires (and another run can start) at most this long after. |
| `retire_source_scopes` | list[string] | `[]` | Incremental runs only: source scopes (a former document_parsing.source_scope value, or the absolute source directory a corpus was indexed from before it moved) whose registry records in this run's index namespace are treated as deleted. The run removes their exclusive artifacts (shared ones are kept) and deletes their records once the removal succeeded. Never the run's own scope. run-ingestion --retire-source-scope adds to this list. |

### `indexing.neptune`

Configuration settings for Neptune graph database indexing

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity_label_prefix` | string (min length 1) | `"Entity"` | Prefix for entity node labels in Neptune |
| `community_label_prefix` | string (min length 1) | `"Community"` | Prefix for community node labels in Neptune |
| `batch_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `100` | Items per Neptune write batch. |
| `index_concurrency` | integer (≥ 1) | `1` | Neptune write batches (and relationship edges, one per request) submitted concurrently; the Gremlin connection pool grows to at least this. Above 1, batches touching the same vertices can raise ConcurrentModificationException; the retry recovers, but the conflicts can make a large run slower than sequential writes, so measure before raising it. |
| `max_attempts` | integer (≥ 1) | `4` | Attempts per Neptune indexer request (writes, read-backs, drops and label clears), including the first, with full-jitter exponential backoff (the wait after attempt n is random between 0 and retry_delay_seconds * 2^(n-1) seconds). Errors a retry cannot fix (malformed query, access denied, bad parameter, read-only violation) fail on the first attempt. 1 disables the retry. |
| `retry_delay_seconds` | integer (≥ 0) | `2` | Base of the retry backoff in seconds (full jitter): the wait after attempt n is random between 0 and retry_delay_seconds * 2**(n-1). 0 retries at once. |
| `property_max_length` | integer (≥ 1) | `4000` | Character cap per Neptune property value. Keep it above the longest description that is not re-summarized (summarization triggers above force_summary_threshold_tokens, 600 tokens or ~2,400 English characters). OpenSearch keeps descriptions in full. Takes effect on re-ingestion. |
| `max_hops` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Depth of the graph expansion around the seed entities at query time. |
| `max_results_per_hop` | integer (≥ 1) | `50` | Maximum number of neighbours one node contributes per traversal hop, so a hub entity cannot fan the expansion out unbounded |
| `entity_importance_source` | `"rank"` \| `"degree"` \| `"none"` | `"rank"` | Graph-expansion relevance orders entities by distance from the seeds (seeds first) and, at the same distance, by this importance: 'rank' (the indexed entity rank, its degree), 'degree' (the entity's edges counted at query time, as MS GraphRAG ranks entities) or 'none' (a neutral 0.5 for every entity, so expansion ranks by distance alone). |
| `traversal_fetch_multiplier` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Graph expansion fetches top_k * retrieval_multiplier * this many entities besides the seeds, split evenly across the seeds, ranks them by relevance, then keeps every seed plus the top top_k * retrieval_multiplier of the others. 1 = no over-fetch: every traversed entity is kept, with no cut after ranking. |

### `indexing.opensearch`

Configuration settings for OpenSearch vector and text indexing

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text_units_index_prefix` | string (min length 1) | `"graphrag-text-units"` | Index name prefix for text unit documents |
| `entities_index_prefix` | string (min length 1) | `"graphrag-entities"` | Index name prefix for entity documents |
| `community_reports_index_prefix` | string (min length 1) | `"graphrag-community-reports"` | Index name prefix for community report documents |
| `build_relationship_vector_index` | boolean | `true` | Build the relationship vector index (embeds Relationship.description). LightRAG mix/hybrid query it for high-level keywords and incident edges, GraphRAG local for its relationship section and bridge relationships, and simple and drift search it with the other indexes; only global does without it. false skips the relationship embeddings at the cost of those. The Neptune relationship edges are indexed either way. |
| `relationships_index_prefix` | string (min length 1) | `"graphrag-relationships"` | Index name prefix for relationship documents (LightRAG global retrieval) |
| `claims_index_prefix` | string (min length 1) | `"graphrag-claims"` | Index name prefix for claim (covariate) documents |
| `extraction_records_index_prefix` | string (min length 1) | `"graphrag-extraction-records"` | Index name prefix for the extraction store: each text unit's extracted entities, relationships and claims, keyed by its text and the extraction settings, so an unchanged chunk is not extracted again (no embeddings). A full build or reset keeps only the records its text units name |
| `default_analyzer` | string (min length 1) | `"standard"` | OpenSearch text analyzer used when the language has no specific mapping |
| `language_analyzers` | dict[string, string] | `{"en": "english", "ko": "nori"}` | Text analyzer per language code (en: english, ko: nori); languages without an entry use default_analyzer. nori needs the analysis-nori plugin, which an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain has only once its optional package is associated (the CDK stack maps ko to cjk). Setting the key replaces the whole map. |
| `refresh_after_batch` | boolean | `true` | Whether to refresh OpenSearch indices after each batch operation for immediate visibility |
| `persist_embedding_cache` | boolean | `false` | Persist the content-hash embedding cache to S3, so unchanged text is not embedded again by a later run (each Fargate task is a fresh process). Requires aws.s3.bucket_name. |
| `embedding_cache_s3_key` | string | `"embedding-cache/cache.json"` | S3 key (under the cache bucket) for the persisted embedding cache when persist_embedding_cache is enabled. |
| `max_query_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `100` | Maximum number of hits returned per OpenSearch query |
| `index_settings` | dict[string, Any] | see `config-template.yaml` | OpenSearch settings of the indices this package creates (number_of_shards, number_of_replicas, refresh_interval, ...); they apply to indices created afterwards. Raise refresh_interval (or set "-1") for faster bulk loads, then reset it for live querying. Setting the key replaces the whole map. |
| `vector_search` | dict[string, Any] | see `config-template.yaml` | HNSW algorithm parameters for approximate nearest neighbor search. ef_search is the candidate list size of a query: on faiss and nmslib the index setting index.knn.algo_param.ef_search (fixed when the index is created), on lucene, which ignores that setting, the k of every kNN query (at least the hits requested), read at query time. |

## `search`

Search configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto_routable_strategies` | list[`"auto"` \| `"drift"` \| `"global"` \| `"local"` \| `"simple"` \| `"mix"` \| `"hybrid"` \| `"naive"`] (min length 1) | `["local", "mix", "global"]` | Strategies the auto router may pick; its prompt describes exactly these, in this order. simple is left out by default because the graph strategies cover its direct lookups with graph context, and drift because it costs up to 27 LLM calls a query (local: 2), a price one misrouted question should not pay; add it to route to it. global and drift are skipped when graph.community_detection.enabled is false (no community reports), and local is used when nothing is left; with one strategy left no router call is made. auto itself is rejected; every strategy stays selectable explicitly. |
| `max_concurrency` | integer (≥ 1) | `10` | LLM calls and sub-searches one query keeps in flight: the global map calls, the dynamic-selection ratings, and the DRIFT primer calls and follow-up local searches. Per query, so concurrent queries (run-eval keeps processing.max_concurrency of them in flight) multiply it; lower it if a query's calls are throttled. |
| `store_timeout_seconds` | number (> 0) | `30.0` | Seconds a query waits for one OpenSearch or Neptune request (and for opening a Neptune connection); a Neptune traversal, including its wait for a pooled connection, gets twice that. A store that does not answer fails the query instead of answering from no context. Ingestion keeps its own, longer limits. |
| `store_max_attempts` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Attempts of one OpenSearch query request that timed out, could not connect or got a 429/502/503/504, including the first, with a jittered backoff between them (0.25-0.5 s, then 0.5-1 s, doubling up to 2-4 s), so a short throttling burst is waited out. A hung cluster fails a query after about store_max_attempts x store_timeout_seconds. Neptune query requests are not retried. |

### `search.hybrid`

Hybrid search configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lexical_weight` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.5` | Weight of the lexical side of a hybrid search. A hybrid search runs a lexical and a kNN search on each index, each fetching at least 50 hits, min-max normalizes each over its hits, takes their weighted mean (lexical_weight, vector_weight) and keeps the requested number, so the ranking does not depend on how many hits a query asks for. |
| `vector_weight` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.5` | Weight for vector search results |

### `search.fusion`

Search result fusion configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | `"rrf"` \| `"weighted"` | `"rrf"` | How results of different sources are fused: rrf (reciprocal rank fusion) or weighted (score-weighted). |
| `rrf_k` | integer (≥ 1) | `60` | The k constant of reciprocal rank fusion: each result adds 1 / (rrf_k + rank). |
| `diversity_lambda` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.5` | MMR lambda for diversity filtering: score = lambda*relevance - (1-lambda)*max_similarity, with relevance min-max normalized to [0, 1] over the fused candidates. 1.0 = pure relevance (no diversity), 0.0 = maximum diversity. Lower values penalize redundant results more strongly. Filtering is skipped at 1.0 (no diversity benefit). |
| `fusion_weights` | dict[string, number] | `{}` | Per-source-bucket weights, applied by both fusion methods: RRF scales each bucket's 1/(rrf_k + rank) term and weighted fusion scales its scores. Keys are the source buckets the search strategies emit: local (graph_entities, text_units, relationships, bridge_relationships, community_reports, claims), LightRAG (lightrag_entities, lightrag_relationships, lightrag_endpoint_entities, lightrag_incident_relationships, lightrag_chunks, lightrag_linked_chunks), simple (opensearch_all), global (opensearch_community_reports, text_units) and drift (results). A bucket without a key weighs 1.0 (the default: none). |

### `search.reranking`

Reranking configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Rerank the fused results with models.rerank. Bedrock rerank models are not offered in every region, and the Rerank API needs its own IAM statement (bedrock:Rerank on Resource '*'). |
| `top_k` | integer (≥ 1) | `100` | Fused candidates sent to the reranker. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Fail the query with RerankModelError when reranking is enabled but the rerank model cannot be built, the rerank call fails or it returns nothing usable. false keeps the fused order and reports the outcome in SearchResult.metadata['rerank']. No effect when reranking is disabled or providers.rerank.kind is none. |

### `search.global_search`

Global search configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `community_depth` | integer (≥ 0) | `2` | The cut of the community hierarchy whose reports global search maps over, counted from the root as MS GraphRAG's community_level (default 2 there too): the communities at this depth plus the leaves above it, so every entity is covered once. 0 = the root communities (fewest, broadest reports); a large value = the leaves. With use_dynamic_selection it bounds only the depths a selection that found nothing relevant rates whole (MS GraphRAG's max_level); relevant reports are followed to the leaves. |
| `max_reports_per_level` | integer (≥ 1) | `100` | Upper bound on the reports one cut (or one step of the dynamic selection) contributes. A cut with more reports gives way to the deepest shallower cut that fits (global_cut_depth in the search metadata); when even the root cut does not fit, to the reports of the cut most similar to the query (a hybrid search restricted to the cut, global_level_capped). At most indexing.opensearch.max_query_size - 1: one store request returns at most max_query_size hits and the cut asks for one more than the cap. Each report costs map-step input tokens. |
| `use_dynamic_selection` | boolean | `false` | MS GraphRAG dynamic community selection instead of a fixed cut: rate the root reports for the query with models.roles.community_relevance, descend into the children of the relevant ones down to the leaves (dropping a parent once a child is relevant), and rate the whole next depth when a depth yields none, down to community_depth. One fast-model call per rated report, search.max_concurrency at a time; the relevant reports are then mapped. Off by default, as in MS GraphRAG. |
| `relevance_threshold` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `0.2` | Dynamic selection keeps a report whose relevance (the 1-10 rating divided by 10) is at least this. 0.2 = anything rated above irrelevant, MS GraphRAG's threshold of 1 on its 0-5 scale: a pruned report prunes its whole subtree. |
| `enable_map_reduce` | boolean | `true` | Map the selected reports into scored key points. false = the reports go to the answer model as they are (budget-trimmed). |
| `map_reduce_min_results` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Minimum community results before map-reduce synthesis is applied; below this the results are returned directly. |
| `map_context_tokens` | integer (≥ 128) | `12000` | Report tokens packed into one map-step LLM call (MS GraphRAG's data_max_tokens, 12000). Reports are packed in order until the next one would exceed it; a longer report gets a call of its own. Map calls run search.max_concurrency at a time. |
| `map_relevance_threshold` | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 100) | `0` | Drop map-step key points whose 0-100 relevance score is at or below this threshold before ranking (0 keeps any positive score). |
| `max_map_reduce_tokens` | integer (≥ 128) | `8000` | Token budget for the ranked key points packed into the reduce step; the highest-scored points are taken until this budget is reached, so the reduce LLM synthesizes from focused, ranked evidence. |
| `reduce_with_llm` | boolean | `false` | Run the reduce step as its own LLM call that summarizes the packed key points, which the answer model then rewrites. Off by default: the packed points go straight to the answer model as one ranked context section, saving one LLM call per query and a second synthesis that can drop facts. |
| `text_unit_slots` | integer (≥ 0) | `0` | Text units of the communities behind the key points added to the context (retrieved for the query and reranked). 0 (default) = none: MS GraphRAG's global context is community reports only, and chunks next to them took most of the answer budget the reports and key points need. Local and mix search cover chunk evidence. |

### `search.local_search`

Local search configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity_frequency_threshold` | integer (≥ 1) | `20` | Drop graph-expanded entities appearing in more than this many text units (too generic to be discriminative for local search) from the context and the text-unit fan-out. The query's own matched (seed) entities are always kept. |
| `include_bridge_relationships` | boolean | `true` | Also fetch the relationships incident to the graph-expanded entities, edges between two of those entities first (MS GraphRAG local's in-network relationships). These bridge edges carry the hops of a multi-hop chain, which the relationship vector query alone often misses. Needs indexing.opensearch.build_relationship_vector_index. false = only the vector query on the relationship index. |

#### `search.local_search.type_quota`

Reserved fusion slots per section type

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text_multiplier` | number (> 0.0) | `2.0` | Chunk slots as a multiple of top_k |
| `text_floor` | integer (≥ 1) | `20` | Minimum chunk slots regardless of top_k |
| `entity_multiplier` | number (> 0.0) | `1.0` | Entity slots as a multiple of top_k |
| `entity_floor` | integer (≥ 1) | `10` | Minimum entity slots regardless of top_k |
| `relationship_multiplier` | number (> 0.0) | `1.0` | Relationship slots as a multiple of top_k |
| `relationship_floor` | integer (≥ 1) | `10` | Minimum relationship slots regardless of top_k |
| `community_multiplier` | number (> 0.0) | `0.5` | Community report slots as a multiple of top_k |
| `community_floor` | integer (≥ 1) | `2` | Minimum community report slots |
| `claim_multiplier` | number (> 0.0) | `0.5` | Claim slots as a multiple of top_k |
| `claim_floor` | integer (≥ 1) | `2` | Minimum claim slots |

### `search.drift_search`

Drift search configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `k_followups` | integer (≥ 1) | `10` | Community reports the primer reads, and follow-up queries run per round (MS GraphRAG drift_k_followups: 20). Each follow-up query is one local search plus one models.roles.drift_action call. |
| `primer_folds` | integer (≥ 1) | `5` | Primer calls the primer reports are split over (MS GraphRAG primer_folds, 5); each drafts its own intermediate answer and follow-up queries. |
| `n_depth` | integer (≥ 1) | `2` | Rounds of follow-up queries (MS GraphRAG n_depth: 3). Up to k_followups * n_depth local searches per query, so the defaults make at most 1 + primer_folds + 20 + 1 = 27 LLM calls (MS GraphRAG's defaults: 67). |
| `local_context_tokens` | integer (≥ 128) | `12000` | Token budget of the local-search context one follow-up query is answered from (MS GraphRAG local_search_max_data_tokens). |
| `max_answer_tokens` | integer (≥ 128) | `8000` | Token budget for the ranked intermediate answers handed to the answer model; the best-scored answers are taken first. |

### `search.lightrag_search`

LightRAG dual-level keyword search configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `raw_query_fallback_max_len` | integer (≥ 0) | `50` | When dual-level keyword extraction yields no keywords, a query whose length is below this (0 disables the gate) falls back to using the raw query as a low-level keyword, mirroring LightRAG. Longer queries skip the fallback to avoid an over-broad graph scan. |
| `kg_stream_top_k` | integer (≥ 1) | `40` | Width of the entity and relationship vector queries (LightRAG's `QueryParam.top_k`, default 40). Separate from the chunk width: collapsing both onto the caller's single top_k starves the graph streams. Acts as a floor — a caller asking for a larger top_k gets it. |
| `chunk_stream_top_k` | integer (≥ 1) | `20` | Width of the chunk stream, and the cap on the merged chunk pool (LightRAG's `QueryParam.chunk_top_k`, default 20). Acts as a floor against the caller's top_k. |
| `related_chunk_number` | integer (≥ 1) | `5` | Chunks allocated per matched entity/relationship when following `text_unit_ids` lineage (LightRAG's `related_chunk_number`). Slots are distributed on a decreasing gradient so the last match still gets one. |
| `enable_graph_expansion` | boolean | `false` | hybrid/mix: also expand the entity hits and relationship endpoints through the Neptune graph (indexing.neptune.max_hops) and add the neighbourhood as entity candidates. Off by default: upstream LightRAG has no multi-hop traversal (its graph context is the matched items plus their one-hop incident edges and endpoint entities, which this strategy already retrieves), and the extra Neptune round trip adds latency and entities less related to the query. |

### `search.token_manager`

Token management configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_context_tokens` | integer \| null (≥ 1024) | `30000` | Retrieval context budget of the answer prompt, in tokens. 30,000 matches upstream LightRAG's total context budget (MS GraphRAG uses 12,000); a budget derived from a 1M-token window (~785K) would never bind, so the per-type budgets would never trim anything. Always clamped to what models.roles.answer_generation accepts beside its output reservation (aws.bedrock.default_max_output_tokens), with a warning. null derives it from that window minus the output reservation and context_window_headroom_ratio. |
| `context_window_headroom_ratio` | number (> 0.0, < 1.0) | `0.1` | Fraction of the answer model's context window held back when deriving max_context_tokens, covering the system prompt, the question, conversation history, and tokenizer estimation error. |
| `token_count_cache_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `1024` | Maximum number of entries in the LRU cache for Bedrock token counting |
| `min_truncated_section_tokens` | integer (≥ 1) | `64` | A section truncated below this many tokens is dropped rather than emitted as an unusable fragment of evidence. |

#### `search.token_manager.type_budgets`

Per-section-type shares of the context window

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | number (≥ 0.0) | `0.5` | Relative share for document chunk sections |
| `entity` | number (≥ 0.0) | `0.2` | Relative share for graph entity sections |
| `relationship` | number (≥ 0.0) | `0.13` | Relative share for graph relationship sections |
| `community` | number (≥ 0.0) | `0.1` | Relative share for community report sections |
| `claim` | number (≥ 0.0) | `0.07` | Relative share for claim (covariate) sections |
| `general` | number (≥ 0.0) | `0.1` | Relative share for untyped sections — global search's map-reduce synthesis lands here. |

## `memory`

Memory system configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_conversations` | integer (≥ 1) | `100` | Conversations held in conversation memory; a new one beyond it drops the one idle longest. |
| `max_messages_per_conversation` | integer (≥ 1) | `20` | Messages kept per conversation; older ones are dropped. |
| `max_conversation_age_hours` | integer (≥ 1) | `168` | Hours a conversation may stay idle (since its last message); an older one is dropped on the next memory lookup and starts over |

## `cache`

Caching system configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ttl_seconds` | integer \| null (≥ 1) | `86400` | Time-to-live of the local stage-cache entries, in seconds; null = never expire. Not applied with --s3-sync, where the bucket lifecycle expires the checkpoints. |

### `cache.chunking`

Configuration for cache data chunking behavior

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Enable cache data chunking for large datasets |
| `chunk_size` | integer (≥ 1) | `1000` | Maximum number of items per cache chunk |
| `max_file_size_mb` | integer (≥ 1) | `50` | Maximum file size in MB before triggering chunking |

### `cache.llm_responses`

Ingestion LLM response cache

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Keep the responses of the ingestion model calls with the run's stage cache, so a re-run with the same pipeline id (after a crash, a stop or a timeout) does not call the model again for a prompt that already answered. Query and evaluation calls are never cached |
| `flush_every` | integer (≥ 1) | `100` | Responses per cache segment file; a segment is written (and uploaded with --s3-sync) when it is full and before each stage checkpoint, so a killed task loses at most this many responses |

## `logging`

Logging system configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | string | `"INFO"` | Log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL. DEBUG logs contain user and corpus text. |
| `log_format` | string | `"structured"` | structured (JSON records, for CloudWatch and other log stores) or plain. |
| `log_to_file` | boolean | `true` | Also write the CLIs' logs to log_file_path (dated per day; a relative path resolves against the working directory). The package configures no handler when imported as a library. |
| `log_file_path` | string (min length 1) | `"logs/log.txt"` | Log file path (CLIs only); relative to the working directory |
| `library_levels` | dict[string, string] | see `config-template.yaml` | Per-logger levels for chatty third-party libraries (logger name -> level). Setting the key replaces the whole map. |

## `observability`

OpenTelemetry tracing configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Emit OpenTelemetry spans for ingestion, queries and evaluation (needs the otel extra). OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true turns it off regardless. |
| `backend` | `"none"` \| `"otlp"` \| `"langfuse"` \| `"phoenix"` | `"none"` | none: spans go to the process's global tracer provider, which a host application or opentelemetry-instrument sets up. otlp: the package installs an OTLP exporter configured by the OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* variables. langfuse / phoenix: the same exporter pointed at Langfuse or Arize Phoenix, with that vendor's attribute names added. |
| `capture_content` | boolean | `false` | Also record prompt and completion text on model spans, and the query and answer on the kg_rag.query span (after redact_patterns). Off by default: spans carry counts, ids and token usage only. Leave it off for confidential corpora. |
| `sample_rate` | number (≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0) | `1.0` | Fraction of root traces sampled (backends otlp, langfuse, phoenix; with 'none' the host's provider samples); child spans follow their parent's decision |
| `service_name` | string (min length 1) | `"unified-kg-rag"` | OpenTelemetry service.name, and the Phoenix project; OTEL_SERVICE_NAME (and PHOENIX_PROJECT_NAME) win when set. |
| `redact_patterns` | list[string] | `[]` | Regular expressions replaced with '[REDACTED]' in captured content and, for the backends this package installs (otlp, langfuse, phoenix), in every exported string attribute, event attribute and status message |
| `export_timeout_seconds` | number (> 0.0, ≤ 60.0) | `10.0` | Upper bound on one span-export request (backends otlp, langfuse, phoenix). OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_TIMEOUT / OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT win when set |

## `evaluation`

Evaluation configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outputs_directory` | string \| path | `"outputs/evaluation"` | Directory the evaluation results are written to. |
| `enabled_evaluators` | list[`"langchain"` \| `"ragas"` \| `"graph_aware"` \| `"retrieval"` \| `"answer_match"`] | see `config-template.yaml` | List of evaluator types to enable for this evaluation run. The deterministic ones (answer_match, retrieval, graph_aware) are free and skip a query that lacks their dataset fields, so they are on by default alongside the LLM judges (langchain, ragas). |
| `langchain_metrics` | list[`"answer_correctness"` \| `"answer_relevancy"` \| `"context_precision"` \| `"context_recall"` \| `"correctness"` \| `"faithfulness"` \| `"partial_correctness"` \| `"entity_coverage"` \| `"relationship_coverage"` \| `"retrieved_entity_coverage"` \| `"retrieved_relationship_coverage"` \| `"answer_length"` \| `"hit_at_k"` \| `"recall_at_k"` \| `"mrr"` \| `"attributable_fraction"` \| `"exact_match"` \| `"token_f1"` \| `"answer_contains"`] | `["correctness", "partial_correctness"]` | Specific evaluation metrics to calculate when using LangChain evaluator. |
| `ragas_metrics` | list[`"answer_correctness"` \| `"answer_relevancy"` \| `"context_precision"` \| `"context_recall"` \| `"correctness"` \| `"faithfulness"` \| `"partial_correctness"` \| `"entity_coverage"` \| `"relationship_coverage"` \| `"retrieved_entity_coverage"` \| `"retrieved_relationship_coverage"` \| `"answer_length"` \| `"hit_at_k"` \| `"recall_at_k"` \| `"mrr"` \| `"attributable_fraction"` \| `"exact_match"` \| `"token_f1"` \| `"answer_contains"`] | see `config-template.yaml` | Specific evaluation metrics to calculate when using RAGAS evaluator. |
| `max_context_tokens` | integer \| null (≥ 1) | `null` | Token cap on the retrieved context passed to the RAGAS judges. null (default) uses the answer model's budget (search.token_manager.max_context_tokens), so faithfulness and context_recall judge the answer against the context it was given; with that budget derived from the model window too, no extra cap applies (the contexts are already the answer model's selection). A value below the answer budget logs a warning: the judge then sees less context than the answer model did. |
| `judge_effort` | `"low"` \| `"medium"` \| `"high"` \| `"xhigh"` \| `"max"` \| null | `"low"` | Reasoning effort for the LLM judge (RAGAS and LangChain evaluators) on adaptive-thinking models (Claude 4.7+). Judge prompts are short extraction/classification calls, so a low effort keeps each metric well inside the RAGAS timeout. null inherits the effort of the judge model's tier (aws.bedrock.default_effort by default). Ignored by models without adaptive thinking. |
| `ragas_timeout` | integer (≥ 1) | `300` | RAGAS RunConfig.timeout in seconds: the budget for scoring ONE metric on ONE sample, covering all of its LLM calls and retries. A timed-out job yields NaN for that metric. RAGAS' own default (180s) is too tight for thinking judges. |
| `ragas_max_contexts` | integer \| null (≥ 1) | `20` | Maximum number of top-ranked retrieved contexts per sample scored by RAGAS context_precision, applied before max_context_tokens. Context precision makes one judge call per context, so its cost scales with the context count; strategies that report 100+ sources time out otherwise. Only that metric is capped (it becomes context_precision@N); faithfulness and context_recall see every context within max_context_tokens, and the answer model's context is unaffected. null disables the cap. |
| `ragas_max_workers` | integer (≥ 1) | `8` | RAGAS RunConfig.max_workers: concurrent metric jobs. Lower it if Bedrock throttles the judge model (throttled calls burn the per-job timeout). |
| `ragas_max_attempts` | integer (≥ 1) | `3` | Total attempts per judge call, including the first (passed as RAGAS RunConfig.max_retries, which RAGAS applies as stop_after_attempt, with exponential backoff). Attempts count against ragas_timeout. |
| `answer_normalization` | `"default"` \| `"official_squad"` | `"default"` | Normalization of the answer_match exact_match and token_f1 scores. 'default' keeps meaning-bearing punctuation (minus signs, decimal points, 'C++') and folds Unicode; 'official_squad' is the official SQuAD v1.1 script (lowercase, ASCII punctuation and English articles removed), so scores compare with published MuSiQue / HotpotQA numbers. answer_contains always uses 'default'. |
| `retrieval_k` | integer (≥ 1) | `5` | Cutoff k for the retrieval evaluator's hit@k / recall@k: the number of top-ranked distinct files (of the reported sources, in rank order) compared with reference_sources. |
| `save_detailed_results` | boolean | `true` | Whether to save detailed evaluation results and reports. |
